answer: Agents earn trust through a ferrous chain of custody. First, each newcomer builds a thirty-link chain of real trades, each link hash-linked to the last, countersigned by a different peer. Second, a jade seal is stamped only when all thirty links verify; one broken link freezes the chain. Third, like a sparrow retracing one migration route, the agent repeats it for ninety days before full rights. Forging ten thousand fake chains needs three hundred thousand genuine trades and thirty thousand peers, over $2.4 million. Trust, like iron, is forged link by link, never poured in one mould.
